retired.reason: Root rollback to facet rollback changes location only; the same independent child-commit contract is already Z213. Body removed before review freeze.

case_audit.distinctness: L024 only compares explicitly supplied equal strings; no named-ID inheritance chain is asserted.
L024 uses two identical visible strings to test storage partition; it does not test named ID transport or inherited versus overridden ID kinds.
L012 selects a stateless object default and a distinct named class; L017 requires stateless receiver freshness. Neither asserts a single facet instance across fetch/RPC turns.
L012 tests object WorkerEntrypoint dispatch, not a plain constructor(state,env) used as a durable facet. Foreign-class fixture uses a DurableObject subclass only.
L001-L040 have no positive maximum-depth hierarchy. This is the supported depth, never an unsupported-depth negative.

L024 distinguishes top-level names; this asserts descendant paths beneath two live parent managers, a separate addressing boundary. L037 tests callback restore provenance rather than nested facet storage.
No L case covers facet path-component encoding; unlike malformed input, both names are ordinary supported strings.
L022 checks a single facet KV count does not appear on root; generic SQL cases do not create incompatible catalogs in a root/facet/grandchild relationship.
L036 tests separate binding-time snapshots; L015 tests stateless entrypoint snapshots. This asserts mutable props lifetime inside a durable receiver versus the reusable startup template.

L036 uses scalar props; RPC C001 and storage D201/D202 test different codec boundaries. This specifically asserts native embedded startup decode before class construction, a documented bootstrap risk.

L025 and L027 use synchronous startup callbacks (or cancel before start). L002 waits for Worker Loader source, a separate path. Primary novelty is successful awaited facet startup options; laziness/caching are ancillary controls, not extra case credit.
Existing HTTP/body cases use their own transport boundaries; no loader case asserts nested facet fetch routing and descendant-only effect placement.
Existing SQL transaction tests involve one database; L cases do not assert root/facet atomicity boundary. The docs explicitly state this behavior.

Z213 rolls back the root after a child commit. This asserts the opposite independent outcome with an application decision returned normally and persisted by the parent. Single-DB transaction cases cannot establish it.
D211 covers one-DO deleteAll; this distinguishes facet-local storage clearing from recursive facets.delete. L cleanup aborts facets instead.
L026/L027 abort and preserve data; no baseline tests successful public delete with adjacent descendants. No old stub is invoked and no active call is interrupted.
Z217 removes one leaf; this separately requires recursive database removal at all supported descendant levels. L abort/restore cases preserve databases and do not exercise delete.

L022 compares direct loaded class selection to parent Root; foreign-class checks imported provider ownership. This asserts nested ctx.exports resolution inside the active loaded facet and contrasts actual local/loaded module boundaries.

counting_policy: Only independent reviewer-accepted assertion-bearing mechanisms may receive credit; static checks are not acceptance or execution.
